working_screening_envelope: T_model <= T_eq under methane 5 ppt baseline
comparison_envelopes: Permafrost depth scenarios 305/610/914 m; geothermal gradients 2.0/3.2/4.0 C per 100 m; hydrostatic pore-pressure gradient 9.795 kPa/m
physical_reason: Methane hydrate is stable only inside a pressure-temperature window.
hydrate_support: Inside the modeled window means hydrate is physically admissible under the stated methane and salinity assumptions.
false_positives_or_masks: Local thermal gradient, abnormal pressure, salinity, gas chemistry, depth-unit error, and source coverage can shift or block the interval.
ml_role: Context, mask, confidence, caveat; not occurrence or saturation.
source_basis: SCIENCE_TO_ML_LOGIC_LADDER; STABILITY_CALCULATION_PLAN; public stability source bundle
public_guardrail: Admissible is not proof; top/base/thickness remain conditional until assumptions and sources are locked.

working_screening_envelope: Relative low GR; no final numeric project cutoff yet
comparison_envelopes: High GR / shale-prone interval is a negative reservoir-quality flag
physical_reason: Natural gamma radiation separates cleaner sand from shale-prone intervals.
hydrate_support: Low GR can support reservoir-quality sand that can host pore-filling hydrate.
false_positives_or_masks: Clean sand without hydrate, radioactive minerals, thin shale laminations, and depth mismatch can mislead.
ml_role: Reservoir gate and input feature; never a hydrate label.
public_guardrail: Low GR supports reservoir quality only when paired with porosity, hydrate-response logs, QC, and stability context.

working_screening_envelope: Hydrate sand: RHOB 2.00-2.30 g/cc; phi 0.20-0.35 v/v; NPHI 0.20-0.35 v/v
comparison_envelopes: Water sand phi 0.25-0.40; gas sand phi 0.25-0.45; shale phi 0.05-0.20 with clay effects
physical_reason: Density and porosity constrain available pore volume and elastic calculations.
hydrate_support: Porous clean sand gives storage capacity for pore-filling hydrate.
false_positives_or_masks: Shale, carbonate, coal, compaction, unit confusion, gas effect, and washout can distort porosity/density.
ml_role: Input feature and equation input with provenance; cross-check with lithology and QC.
public_guardrail: Porosity supports storage; it does not prove hydrate.

working_screening_envelope: Directional separation; no final numeric cutoff yet
comparison_envelopes: NMRPHI can be an input if measured; NMR_SAT is target/calibration only
physical_reason: NMR distinguishes mobile pore-fluid response and can support independent saturation estimates.
hydrate_support: NMR-density separation or NMR-derived saturation can support hydrate interpretation.
false_positives_or_masks: Missing NMR, clay-bound water, processing settings, and depth mismatch can mislead.
ml_role: NMRPHI may be input; NMR_SAT/Sgh/Sh are Y-only target or calibration references.
public_guardrail: NMR-derived saturation labels must never enter X_allowed.

comparison_envelopes: Water sand 1-5; gas sand 10-100+; ice/frozen 100-1000+; shale 1-10; clay-rich 0.5-5
physical_reason: Hydrate replaces conductive pore water and can raise formation resistivity.
hydrate_support: Higher Rt in clean porous sand can support hydrate response.
false_positives_or_masks: Free gas, ice, tight rock, carbonates/cement, salinity assumptions, invasion, shale correction, and washout can also raise or distort resistivity.
ml_role: Log-transform and combine with lithology, porosity, elastic features, QC, and stability context.
public_guardrail: High resistivity alone is not hydrate proof.

comparison_envelopes: Water sand 2.0-3.0; gas sand 1.5-2.5; ice/frozen 3.0-4.2; shale 2.5-4.5
physical_reason: Hydrate can stiffen the sediment frame and raise compressional velocity.
hydrate_support: Higher Vp with clean sand and Vs support can indicate hydrate-bearing sediment.
false_positives_or_masks: Ice, cement, carbonate, compaction, competent lithology, stress, and unit conversion can mimic high Vp.
ml_role: Measured input and source for impedance and elastic moduli.
public_guardrail: Velocity needs unit provenance and elastic/lithology cross-checks.

working_screening_envelope: Hydrate sand Vs: 1.0-2.5 km/s; G: 5-25 GPa; mu-rho: 10-55 GPa*g/cc
comparison_envelopes: Gas sand Vs 0.3-1.0 and G 0.5-5; water sand Vs 0.5-1.5 and G 1-10
physical_reason: Hydrate increases rigidity; free gas does not stiffen the frame the same way.
hydrate_support: Higher Vs and rigidity support hydrate-related frame stiffening.
false_positives_or_masks: Ice, cement, carbonate, lithology, stress, and missing shear sonic can mimic or block the signal.
ml_role: Input feature and source for mu-rho, shear modulus, and Vp/Vs.
public_guardrail: Rigidity is strong support only when reservoir, resistivity, QC, and stability context agree.

working_screening_envelope: Hydrate broad screening range: 1.6-2.4; tighter crossplot hypothesis: 1.4-1.6 pending calibration
physical_reason: The ratio captures coupled compressional and shear behavior.
hydrate_support: Hydrate can trend toward stiffer lower-ratio behavior than gas in some contexts.
false_positives_or_masks: Strong overlap among gas, water, shale, ice, lithology, and stress effects.
ml_role: Derived crossplot feature; useful only with source curves and context.
public_guardrail: Use broad range for screening; tighter range is only a hypothesis until calibrated.

physical_reason: Impedance and elastic attributes combine density and velocity behavior.
hydrate_support: Hydrate-bearing sand can show higher stiffness/impedance and rigidity contrast.
false_positives_or_masks: Compaction, lithology, cement, carbonate, stress, unit errors, bad density, or bad velocity can mimic contrast.
ml_role: Derived feature with inherited provenance; crossplot and model input after unit checks.
public_guardrail: Elastic attributes inherit all density and velocity caveats.

working_screening_envelope: Coverage-first QC; no final washout threshold until bit size, unit, and sign convention are confirmed
comparison_envelopes: If missing, create missing-QC flag rather than pretending a filter was applied
physical_reason: Borehole size controls whether density, neutron, sonic, and resistivity logs are trustworthy.
hydrate_support: In-gauge intervals support use of the other curves.
false_positives_or_masks: Washout, rugosity, tool standoff, bit-size reference errors, and sign convention errors corrupt logs.
ml_role: QC exclusion, downweighting, or missingness flag; not hydrate evidence.
public_guardrail: Caliper is a trust gate, not a hydrate signal.

comparison_envelopes: Saturation field authority and fraction-vs-percent policy pending
physical_reason: Targets supervise training and validation rather than describing independent input evidence.
hydrate_support: Occurrence and saturation labels provide ground truth only after approved source authority is locked.
false_positives_or_masks: Using target columns as predictors creates leakage and fake performance.
ml_role: Y-only target, calibration, validation, and residual review; never X_allowed.
public_guardrail: Targets must never enter the feature matrix.
